hook.title: Hiding roads from the traveller
hook.text: You want a model that can predict *missing roads*. There are no ready-made labels, so you **make your own game**: hide some existing roads, show the traveller the remaining map, and ask “is there a road here?” for pairs including the hidden ones. The key rule: the hidden roads (the answers) must **never** appear on the map you show, otherwise the traveller just copies them.
hook.recall: Remember hiding roads: supervision edges are the hidden answers and are never fed to the GNN; message edges form the map the GNN passes messages over.

explore.intro: Click edges to turn them into supervision edges (gold) or back into message edges (blue).
tasks: Hide two edges. How many message edges remain?
What happens if you hide almost every edge?
explore.takeaway: Link prediction is unsupervised/self-supervised: we create labels and splits ourselves. **Message edges** feed the GNN; **supervision edges** are the targets and are *not* fed into the GNN.
